text:
tara: quick follow-up from the multi-region RFC: we need a concrete fallback contract when a resident-region primary is unreachable. do we block, queue, or proxy-to-standby with consent? need a single-line decision + owners.

ev an: spelling: evan :) we discussed three behaviors in the RFC but never landed on defaults. ops says blocking is easiest, infra prefers escrow to preserve SLA.

maria: From product: customers want availability but also auditable consent. can we offer a tiered policy? default strict, paid opt-in for cross-region soft-handoff.

legal-bot: Regs: EU residency requires processing and storage within EU unless explicit consent exists. Consent must be recorded (who/when/scope) and revocable.

ops-bot: runbook note: if we forward writes to non-resident standby we must mark them "temporarily accepted" and surface queue depth/age. add an operator circuit-breaker if queue_age > 5m or depth > 10k.

devx: API suggestion: add header X-Residence-Policy: fail|consent-forward|escrow. default=fail. also return metadata in 4xx describing missing consent.

tara: engineering question: if we escrow accepts in standby, how to guarantee single-apply when EU primary returns? do we require client idempotency keys?

ev an: yes, require request_id or idempotency_key. escrow record = {request_id, origin_region, tenant, payload_hash}. reconciliation uses request_id to dedupe.

maria: Billing: if standby executes generation, we bill that execution. reconciliation shouldn't double-bill. add a flag to billing pipeline to mark reconciled requests as billed_already=true.

sam.k: what about cache and embedding replicas? if we accept in standby, embeddings may replicate to global store violating residency. need to gate replication until finality.

maria: good catch. embeddings for resident tenants should be labeled and replication is blocked until reconciliation finalizes. that will add latency to search across regions. inform customers.

legal-bot: add consent token format: consent_id, timestamp, scope_list (processing, storage, analytics). retention: 7 years audit log.

ops-bot: metrics to add: residency_forward_rate, escrow_accept_rate, escrow_reconciliation_failures, consent_check_latency_ms.

devx: sample error payload to standardize: ```{
  "error":"RESIDENCY_VIOLATION",
  "code":"RESIDENCY_BLOCKED",
  "details":"Tenant policy: EU-only. No consent on record."
}```

maria: decision proposal: default = fail (fail-fast), enterprise opt-in = consent-forward with escrow, non-PII opt-in = direct-forward with client-warning header. feedback?

evan: +1 to that hybrid. keeps legal safe by default, offers tiers.

tara: +1. I'll write the RFC patch: add config flag residency.default_policy and tenant flag residency.cross_region_optin.

sam.k: owners: tara = RFC patch; devx = API header PR; evan = runtime escrow implementation; ops-bot = runbook metrics; legal-bot = consent schema. deadlines: RFC patch by next Tue, runtime spike in 2w.

maria: will update pricing doc for standby billing rules.

ops-bot: noting link to runbook template: https://go/runbooks/residency-escrow

tara: thanks everyone. closing when RFC PR lands. short tech spike scheduled next Fri.
